blocks.intro: Disposal work in Geneva varies with the age of the kitchen.

items.h3: First Disposal in an Older Kitchen
items.body: Some kitchens in historic homes never had one. We check the drain, the dishwasher connection and the power under the sink before quoting.

items.h3: Old Drain Lines Under the Sink
items.body: A new disposal can expose a corroded drain arm in an older home. We check it while we're there.
In homes built after 1990, replacing an old disposal is usually quick.

blocks.h2: Garbage Disposal Questions From Geneva Homeowners

items.q: Can you add a disposal to a kitchen that never had one?
items.answer: Usually. We check the drain size, the dishwasher hookup and whether there's a switched outlet. If power is needed, we'll tell you before the install.

items.preview: Jams and connections are repairs. A leaking body or dead motor means replace.
items.answer: A jam, a tripped reset or a loose connection can be fixed. A leaking housing or burned-out motor means replacement.

items.q: What shouldn't go down a disposal?
items.preview: Grease, bones, fibrous scraps, coffee grounds, eggshells, rice and pasta.
items.answer: Grease and oil, bones, fibrous scraps, coffee grounds, eggshells, rice and pasta.
Many last around 8 to 15 years, depending on the model and use.

items.q: Why does my sink drain slowly with a new disposal?
items.preview: The drain line behind it may be old and narrowed.
items.answer: In older homes, the drain arm behind the sink can be narrowed by years of buildup. A new disposal sends food into it faster. Cleaning or replacing that section fixes it.

items.q: How much does disposal installation cost in Geneva?
items.preview: It depends on the unit. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the unit and any plumbing or electrical changes. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
